content: ITP (Interval Testing Procedure, Pini & Vantini 2016, Biometrics) returns a p-value vector (one value per basis component) after closure adjustment. Key concepts: (1) adjusted_pvalues — the closure-adjusted p-value curve, length n_basis; (2) raw_pvalues — pre-adjustment; (3) detection vs localisation: detection = does ANY adjusted_pvalue < alpha (global rejection); localisation = WHICH basis intervals have adjusted_pvalue < alpha (identifying where in the functional domain differences occur). Scalar reductions of the vector-valued p-curve: (a) min_adjusted_pvalue = min(adjusted_pvalues) — global detection scalar, equivalent to minimum p-value in the curve; this is the most natural single-number summary for overall significance; (b) n_significant_intervals = count(adjusted_pvalues < alpha) for a given alpha; (c) proportion_significant = n_significant_intervals / n_basis — fraction of domain showing significant difference; (d) first_significant_basis = index of first basis coefficient with adjusted_pvalue < alpha — localises the onset of effects; (e) basis_type string and n_basis int provide context. The localisation/detection distinction: detection (min_adjusted_pvalue < alpha) answers 'is there any difference?'; localisation (proportion_significant, first_significant_basis) answers 'where is the difference?'. This distinction maps directly to two separate advisor interpretations. Grounding constraint: all scalars computed from the fdars-returned adjusted_pvalues numpy array — no LLM inference about specific intervals.
